post.description: One sign-in for everyone: the supervisor gets the panel session (kind admin), a user gets their own page (kind user, a separate cookie). Needs the X-Meridian: 1 header. With two-factor sign-in, the first answer is {totp_required: true}; send the same request again with code.

A challenge for any of this panel's passkeys: pass options.publicKey to navigator.credentials.get() and send the answer to finish within five minutes. Needs the X-Meridian: 1 header, and the panel opened at its own name (passkeys do not work at an IP address).

Signs the passkey's account in, without a two-factor code: a passkey checks the person (user verification) and the device. A passkey whose counter went back - perhaps copied - is refused. Needs the X-Meridian: 1 header.

get.summary: Panel name, and for signed-in callers version and protocol catalogue

post.description: Signs out every other session.
Options for navigator.credentials.create() (options.publicKey): a passkey kept on the device or by its provider, with user verification. At most 20 per account.

post.summary: Add the passkey the browser made

post.description: The token is returned once. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Where traffic went, by bytes then connections (at most 500). Bytes are exact for WireGuard; Xray and Hysteria2 report connections.

post.description: Returns the install command to run on the server. protocols lists what to set up once the agent connects.

delete.description: The agent removes everything Rosélune set up and uninstalls itself. Everyone on the server is disconnected.

post.description: The agent cannot reach the panel until it is reinstalled with the new command. Traffic is not affected.

post.summary: Share a server with another panel
post.description: The other panel adds the server as shared with it and gives you a share code; with it, this server's agent reports to that panel too and runs what it sets up - protocols, users, forwards, traffic rules - but never the console. The host stays yours: the agent's and the cores' upgrades, the country rule, relaying, scans. Ports and WireGuard networks already used here are refused to it. Two panels at most; needs agent 1.0 (caps.share). The answer is the action's id (GET /api/actions/{id}).

delete.summary: Stop sharing a server with a panel
delete.description: What that panel ran on the server is removed and its users there are disconnected. A panel the server is shared with leaves by removing the server on its side.

post.description: Queues an explicit maintenance action. restart_pending restarts exactly what waits for a restart (the server's pending_restart) and disconnects those users for a moment; restart_all restarts everything that carries traffic - Xray, Hysteria2, each user's own server (mieru, Snell, AnyTLS), realm forwards - and then the agent, so everyone on the server reconnects once (agent 1.3.1 and later); restart_xray and upgrade_xray disconnect Xray users for a moment; upgrade_hysteria and upgrade_realm switch the server to the version in Settings and restart those cores (their users reconnect); upgrade_agent disconnects nobody.

get.description: Processor, memory, disk, disk activity, network, load, connections and temperature over time, and the ping monitors it measures. Kept two days a minute at a time and a month in five-minute steps; a missing point means the server did not report.

get.summary: Addresses the servers measure the way to
get.description: Each round sends three probes - ICMP echo, or TCP connections - from every server that measures it; the latest round and the last hour's loss are included per server.

post.description: The servers start measuring within seconds; rounds measured while a server cannot reach the panel are delivered later. At most 20.

patch.description: Only the given fields change. What it measured so far is kept.

get.description: Protocols with their transports and security layers, the apps the panel writes subscriptions for, and the choices for fingerprints, XHTTP modes and certificates.

post.summary: Check a protocol before adding it
post.description: Says whether the combination can be saved (and if not, why and what to do instead), how apps will name it, its usual ports, which apps can use it and what the admin needs to do. Nothing is stored.

post.summary: Add a protocol to a server
post.description: Applied live without restarting anything. Only combinations that work can be saved (POST /api/protocols/check shows why one cannot). Port 0 picks a free common port. REALITY camouflage is checked from the server.

patch.description: Only the given fields change; the result must still be a working combination. Changing the transport, security or certificate means devices must refresh their subscription.

post.description: New REALITY keys, self-signed certificate, Shadowsocks server key or WireGuard key. Every device using the protocol must refresh its subscription.

post.summary: Check a REALITY camouflage site from the server

get.description: Every user with how they have it: all (everything, including new servers), server (the whole server, with protocols added later), protocol (this one) or none.

put.summary: Give a protocol to users, or take it from them
put.description: In one step. Users who have it already, or do not have it, are left as they are. Taking it from users who have it through everything or the whole server needs split=true: their access is written out as the servers and protocols they have now, less this one, and they no longer get new ones by themselves (409 without it). Users who lose it are disconnected from it; applied live.

post.summary: Look for proxy software already on the server
post.description: The agent reads (and changes nothing) the configs of Xray, V2Ray, 3x-ui and x-ui, sing-box and Hysteria2. Poll the action, then GET the scan.

get.description: Programs, their protocols, ports and user names, and whether each can be imported. Keys and passwords are never shown.

post.summary: Import protocols found by the scan
post.description: Each detected user becomes a Rosélune user (or is matched by name) and keeps their credentials, keys and certificate. With take_over the old service is stopped and the same ports are served, so devices keep working; without it nothing is stopped and busy ports are moved.

get.summary: List shared certificates, the protocols using each and where each server stands with it
A shared certificate, with per-server status

patch.summary: Rename or replace a shared certificate - one call updates every server that uses it (for renewal hooks)

delete.summary: Remove a shared certificate that no protocol uses

get.summary: The Xray configuration a server gets, with your code merged in (users left out)

post.description: Each user gets a subscription link and, unless sign_in is false, a username and password for their own page. A generated password is returned once. count > 1 creates name-01, name-02, ... A user who uses up their quota is suspended by itself (status out_of_data) until their data starts over - the next reset, a higher quota, a new period on a plan or reset-usage; expiry and the IP limit only raise alerts.

patch.description: Only the given fields change. A new username or password signs the user out everywhere; an empty username removes the sign-in.

post.summary: Pause, resume, new link, new credentials, reset usage, sign out or new password
post.description: pause disconnects every device now; resume lets them back (a user whose data is used up stays out until it starts over); rotate-link replaces the link (old one stops working); reset-keys gives new credentials (devices must refresh); reset-usage zeroes this cycle (a user whose data was used up can connect again at once); sign-out ends the user's sessions on their own page; new-password generates a sign-in password (and a username if there is none) and returns it once.

post.summary: Start a new period on a preset plan
post.description: Copies the plan's quota, counting, reset, device and speed limits and access into the user, starting at starts_at (default now) and ending after the plan's duration. Usage starts at zero unless reset_usage is false. Changing the plan later changes nobody unless it is saved with update_users.

get.description: Templates for users: a quota and what counts toward it, how long it lasts, resets, device and speed limits and access.

patch.description: Only the given fields change. With update_users, the users on this plan take its new quota, counting, reset, limits and access too (their start and end dates stay); otherwise nobody changes.

delete.description: Its users keep what it gave them.

get.summary: IPs that used this user's link
The signed-in user's link, limits, devices and usage per server

post.description: Signs the user out everywhere else.

get.description: Up to two Telegram accounts check the user's usage with the bot and open their page in its Mini App, while the supervisor allows it (telegram_user_link).

post.summary: A code that links a Telegram account
post.description: Sent to the bot (/link CODE, or the t.me link), it links the Telegram account that sends it. It works once, for ten minutes.

delete.summary: The user unlinks a Telegram account
delete.description: Once a month (30 days). Not from a sign-in made in the Mini App: in a browser, signed in with the password - or /unlink in the bot.

post.summary: Open the Mini App for a linked Telegram account
post.description: With the launch data Telegram signed (Telegram.WebApp.initData, at most an hour old): a linked user gets a session for their own page, the supervisor's linked account one for the panel (that cannot change passwords, two-factor, API tokens, sessions, the console, plugins or the site rule). Unlinked: linked=false - sign in once with POST /api/tg/link.

post.summary: Link the Telegram account by signing in once
post.description: The username and password (and the supervisor's two-factor code) of the account to link, with the Mini App's launch data. Guarded like the sign-in page: addresses that keep failing are shut out, a username many fail at slows down, and a Telegram account gets five tries an hour. An account has two Telegram accounts at most.

delete.description: Any link, at any time (users themselves may unlink once a month). That Telegram account no longer opens anything; its sessions made in the Mini App stay until they are signed out.

post.summary: A code that links one of your Telegram accounts
post.description: Needs "Open the panel from Telegram" (telegram_panel). Send it to the bot (/link CODE); it works once, for ten minutes.

get.summary: Every server for the live dashboard
get.description: The status page's dashboard: servers (name, place, public IP addresses, up or down, availability over 24 hours and 30 days, throughput, load, memory, disk, connections, monthly bandwidth and traffic, expiry date, system), totals, traffic per day and outages. Visitors get it while the status page shows the servers to everyone; the supervisor always. IP addresses are in it only while the status page shows them (status_ips, off by default) - then for everyone, otherwise for nobody. Nothing about users, protocols, ports, keys or prices.

get.summary: Throughput per server since a time
A server's charts for its details
get.description: As GET /api/servers/{id}/series, for whoever may see the status page's servers: visitors and users get the charts in status_charts and the ping monitors marked public, without their addresses or how many people are connected; the supervisor gets all of them.

get.summary: Cities for setting a server's location by hand
Country rules for the servers and for this site
get.description: Both rules, what each server follows, devices connected now by country, packets the servers' rule refused today and requests this site refused.

put.description: block refuses the listed countries; allow admits only them. It covers every protocol and forward (SSH is never touched), applies within seconds and also cuts connections that are already open. Servers with their own rule (PATCH /api/servers/{id} country_mode) keep it. Private networks and the panel's own servers always get in.

put.summary: Set who may open this site
put.description: The same kind of rule for the panel, the users' pages, the status page and subscription links. Agents are never refused. A rule that would lock out the address you send it from is refused.

get.summary: External nodes: proxies elsewhere, usable as exits
get.description: Each with what uses it (protocols passing through it, rules, load balancers). Credentials are never shown again (only servers get them, in their configuration).

post.description: From share links (vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss:// - Shadowsocks and Shadowsocks 2022 -, hysteria2:// or hy2://, wireguard://, https:// proxies), a subscription's base64 content, Clash / mihomo YAML, or a subscription address fetched once (https only, public addresses only). Every entry that cannot be used comes back with the reason - nodes that turn certificate checks off or send traffic unencrypted are refused, as are kinds a server's Xray cannot connect to (TUIC, AnyTLS, ...) and names inside a local network. Nodes already imported are skipped; a name that is taken gets a number (HK, HK 2). At most 2000 nodes per import and per account, 4 MB of text.

patch.summary: Rename, turn on or off, or give an external node a new link
patch.description: Turned off, protocols and rules that use it block their traffic until it is on again - they never leave from their own server instead. A new link moves their traffic at once. Names are unique (409 otherwise).

delete.description: Protocols that passed through it and rules that sent traffic there block it until they get another exit; load balancers lose it as a member. Its id is never used again.

post.summary: Check an external node from a server
post.description: The server's agent (1.0 or later) opens a connection to the node - and, behind TLS or REALITY, makes a TLS handshake checked against its server name - and reports whether that worked and how long it took (output of GET /api/actions/{id}: ok, addr, ms, tls, error). Nothing passes through the node. Hysteria2 and WireGuard nodes speak UDP and are refused.

get.summary: Subscription links: providers' subscriptions read again on a schedule
get.description: Each with its nodes (external nodes that follow it), when it was last read and why that failed if it did, the entries it could not use, what the provider says about the subscription (traffic, expiry) and the load balancers that use all of its nodes.

post.description: Read at once and then every every_hours hours (https only, public addresses only, 4 MB at most). Share links, base64, Clash / mihomo YAML and sing-box configurations are read alike; each node is written into Rosélune's own form, so every app gets it in a form it understands. Its nodes become external nodes that follow the provider: new ones are added, changed ones updated in place (rules and protocols keep using them), and ones that left are removed - or kept, marked, while a protocol, rule or load balancer still names them. A refresh that fails, or finds no usable node, changes nothing. offer gives the nodes to users too (not WireGuard: one key cannot serve many devices); Rosélune cannot count or limit what goes through them. The link is saved even when the first read fails (error says why).

patch.description: A new address, prefix or filter reads it again at once. Turned off, it is not read and its nodes cannot be used: what uses them is blocked until it is on again.

delete.description: With ?keep_nodes=1 its nodes stay, as nodes imported once; otherwise they go too, and protocols and rules that used them block their traffic until they get another exit. Load balancers lose it as a member.

post.summary: Read a subscription link again now
post.description: At most 20 times an hour.

get.summary: Traffic splitting: rules, load balancers and the exits they can use
get.description: Rules apply in order to the Xray protocols (VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, SOCKS5, HTTP) of every server, some servers or some protocols; the first that matches sends the traffic directly, through a proxy pass (a protocol on another server or an external node), to a load balancer, or blocks it. What no rule takes leaves as before. On the exit protocol's own server the traffic leaves the way that protocol's own traffic does. Traffic passing through a server from other servers never follows its rules. problems lists what does not work as written and on which servers (that traffic is blocked there, never sent directly instead), rules that reach nothing, and site lists or countries Xray refused.

post.description: Applied live on every server it covers; nothing restarts. Sites are Xray site lists (geosite); countries and addresses match connections made to an address - most apps send names, which sites and domains match, so use both for a country. A rule holds at most 2000 entries, all rules together 10000.

patch.description: Only the given fields change; match is replaced as a whole. Servers or protocols that were removed since stay out of the rule, and an exit that was removed may stay as it is (its traffic stays blocked).

put.summary: Put the rules in a new order

post.description: Its members - protocols on your servers, external nodes, or direct - share the traffic rules send to it: at random, taking turns, or the fastest first (Xray then checks every member each minute; that starts with one Xray restart on each server it is used on, shown as restart needed and done on a click - until then it picks at random). On a member protocol's own server, that member leaves the way the protocol's own traffic does. Applied live.

delete.description: Refused while a rule sends traffic to it.

get.summary: What the servers' health checks found
get.description: Signs that a server was broken into or is abused - crypto-miners, programs in temporary folders, new ports, accounts, SSH keys, scheduled tasks, services, kernel modules, SSH sign-ins, unexplained traffic, Rosélune's programs changed - most serious first. Nothing is ever stopped or blocked because of a risk: they only tell.

post.summary: Take the protective step a risk offers
post.description: Does what the risk's fix says (stop a process and quarantine its program, remove an SSH key, lock an account, turn a service off, move a file into quarantine, make SSH take keys only, block addresses from SSH) - the fix as the server's agent proposed it, which checks it all again before it acts. A person confirms it in the panel: browser sessions only, never an API token. A step done marks the risk acknowledged. Poll the step (GET /api/protections) for how it went.

Puts back what the step changed: a file or program from quarantine, the SSH key, the account unlocked, the service on again, SSH taking passwords, the addresses allowed. A stopped process stays stopped. Browser sessions only.

expected: this is yours - it is never flagged again on this server (scope all: on any server, future ones included). acknowledged: seen - it is flagged again if it happens again. open: flag it again. Who decided and when is kept.

get.summary: A server's health check: when it last scanned, and everything it found

post.description: Applies to every protocol and forward on every server and drops open connections. SSH and other services are not affected.

put.description: Send only the fields to change; the others keep their values. Core version changes never restart servers - upgrade each server explicitly.

The raw image as the body: SVG, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 128 KB and 2048 x 2048 pixels. It replaces the built-in umbrella everywhere - top bar, sign-in, loading screens, status page, subscription pages and the browser tab. SVGs may only draw (no scripts, links or outside resources): the answer says what to remove otherwise.

delete.summary: Use the built-in umbrella logo again

get.summary: Notifications: where they go and what is sent
get.description: The bot token and the webhook come back masked - they are never shown again in full.

put.description: New events of the chosen groups are sent as they happen, in order; turning notifications on never sends the past. Omitted fields keep their value; an empty token or webhook removes it. Webhooks must be HTTPS. Nothing is ever paused by them - they only tell. The Telegram bot can also answer commands in the chat, send a daily report and - only with telegram_changes - decide about health risks and pause or resume users, each after a confirmation button; it never sends links, passwords, keys, tokens or the servers' addresses. telegram_changes is turned on, and telegram_users changed, only from a signed-in browser (API tokens get 403); a new bot token or chat turns telegram_changes off, and removing Telegram stops the bot.

post.summary: Send a test message through every channel that is set up
Chats that wrote to the bot lately
post.description: Send the bot a message (or add it to a group) first; then pick the chat from this list instead of looking up its id. The body may carry a token that is not saved yet.

post.summary: Send the Telegram daily report now
post.description: The same report the bot sends each day at telegram_report_hour: traffic today and this month per server and top users, availability, servers offline, paid periods and access ending soon, data running out, open health risks.

A root shell on the server, in the browser: the server's agent starts it and connects it to the panel. From the supervisor's signed-in browser only - never an API token; the password is asked when it was not confirmed in the last 30 minutes. Then open the WebSocket in url from the same page and send ticket first. Opening is in the timeline and the security notifications; nothing typed or shown is kept.

get.description: Binary messages, each starting with its kind: 0 = what is typed (to the server) or printed (from it), 1 = the window's size (cols, rows: two big-endian uint16), 3 = the end ({"exit": code} or {"error": ...}), 4 = the shell is there. The first message from the browser is the ticket. Only from the panel's own page (Origin).
Where backups go, when, how many are kept, and how the last one went. Passwords, keys and the passphrase are never shown.

put.description: Only the given fields change. Destinations are HTTPS only. Backups that leave the panel are encrypted with the passphrase (age): without it they cannot be opened.

post.description: Writes a small file there, lists the folder and removes the file again.
An encrypted backup to the destination; the oldest beyond keep are removed.
A ZIP of the database and the plugins' files - every key and credential the panel has, so your password is asked. With a passphrase the file is encrypted (age -d opens it too).

Either a file (multipart/form-data: password, passphrase, file) or a backup at the destination (JSON). The backup is checked, staged, and the panel restarts with it (needs a service manager that starts it again, as the installer sets up); what it replaces is kept. Servers keep running and get the restored configuration when they reconnect.

get.description: CSS added last to the panel and to the status page and users' pages.

put.description: At most 64 KB each. Style sheets cannot load anything from other sites (the pages' Content-Security-Policy), so CSS changes looks only. The status page's reaches every visitor.

get.summary: Cloudflare Turnstile on the sign-in pages
get.description: Whether every sign-in must pass Turnstile, and the widget's site key. The secret key is never shown.

put.summary: Set up Cloudflare Turnstile for sign-ins
put.description: Keys and on/off, from the browser only. Turning it on (or changing keys while on) needs a token from the widget shown with those keys on this site: Cloudflare must accept it first, so wrong keys never lock the sign-in. MERIDIAN_NO_TURNSTILE=1 on the panel's host turns it off again.

get.summary: Dynamic DNS through Cloudflare: whether a token is saved, and the names it keeps up to date
get.description: The token is never shown.

put.summary: Save or remove the Cloudflare API token
put.description: The token needs the permission Zone - DNS - Edit for the zones of your servers' names. With it, a server whose IP address changes (ddns) can have the panel keep its name's A and AAAA records pointing at it (ddns_cloudflare). Never returned, logged or written into an event; set from the browser only.

post.summary: Try a Cloudflare token without changing anything
post.description: Says, for each name (the one given, or those of the servers that use Cloudflare), which zone it is in, what A and AAAA records it has now, or why the token cannot change it.

get.summary: The panel's public address as servers reach it
get.description: What the host of the public URL resolves to. A server with IPv6 only needs an IPv6 address there (an AAAA record) to install its agent and report, unless its provider carries IPv6 to IPv4 for it (NAT64): note says so when it has none.

get.summary: Updates: this panel's version, the newest release, and servers with an older agent

post.summary: Look for a new release now

post.description: The panel downloads the release, checks its signature (Rosélune's release key) and checksum, backs up the database and hands it to the updater service, which checks it again and installs it. Proxies keep running; the panel restarts once. With agents (the default), every server's agent is upgraded afterwards - nobody is disconnected. Needs a panel installed with install-panel.sh.

Each online server with agent 1.3.1 or later restarts everything that carries traffic - Xray, Hysteria2, each user's own server (mieru, Snell, AnyTLS), realm forwards - with what waited for a restart, and then its agent. Everyone connected anywhere is disconnected once and reconnects by themselves within seconds. Use it after upgrading agents so strict mode counts long connections as they happen. Servers left out are named with the reason (skipped).

post.summary: Upgrade every server's agent to this panel's version
post.description: Only servers whose agent differs from the panel's are upgraded; offline ones as soon as they connect. Agents restart themselves; the proxies keep running and nobody is disconnected. An upgrade that still waits with other binaries is replaced; servers left out are named with the reason (skipped).

get.summary: The uploaded logo (404 while the built-in one is used)
Installed plugins: what each brings, asks for and may do, and how it runs

post.description: The plugin's zip as the body (at most 20 MB): plugin.json at its top, and the files it names. Every path must stay inside the plugin, links and special files are refused, and sizes are limited. A new plugin is installed turned off. A plugin with the same id must be updated with PUT instead.

put.summary: Upload a new version of a plugin
put.description: The zip must be the same plugin (the same id). A plugin that is on keeps running with the new version, unless it asks for more than was agreed to: then it is turned off until the supervisor agrees.

delete.summary: Remove a plugin, its files and its own data

post.description: Agrees to everything the plugin asks for: send its asks list exactly as GET /api/settings/plugins shows it (with the warnings that say what it lets the plugin do). Its styles and scripts load from now on and its program starts.
Its program stops; its styles, scripts, pages, tools and filters are gone at once. If it changed what servers run, they get the panel's own configuration again.

get.summary: What a plugin's program wrote lately
The browser tab icon: the uploaded logo, or the built-in one
A subscription, in the format the app needs
get.description: The app is detected from its User-Agent; ?client= forces a format. Browsers get a page with QR codes and import buttons. Headers carry Subscription-Userinfo (usage, quota, expiry).

post.description: Streamable HTTP transport (JSON-RPC 2.0, JSON responses, stateless). Needs an API token; read-only tokens only see read tools. Tools that disconnect people require confirm=true.

token.description: API token from Settings › API & MCP

user.description: A user's session on their own page
user.name: mrd_u

kind.description: admin (the supervisor: the panel) or user (the user's own page)

totp_required.description: Send the request again with code

ceremony.description: Send it back with the passkey's answer, within five minutes; it works once

options.description: For the browser: navigator.credentials.create() or .get() takes options.publicKey (binary fields are base64url)

about.description: The line the status page shows under its title

user_url.description: Where users sign in to their own page. Signed-in callers only

kinds.description: Protocols the panel can set up. Signed-in callers only

reality_targets.description: Suggested REALITY camouflage sites. Signed-in callers only

engine.description: xray | hysteria | wireguard | solo (mieru, Snell, AnyTLS: a process and a port per user)

transports.description: Transports this protocol can run over

cdn.description: Can run behind a CDN that adds TLS

secret.description: Base32 key for the authenticator app

url.description: otpauth:// URL (render as a QR code)

name.description: What the supervisor called it, e.g. the device it is on

last_used_ip.description: Where its last sign-in came from

synced.description: Backed up by its provider (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager, a password manager): it works on the person's other devices too
